chapter_title: Chương 79: Nhật Ký Tốt Nghiệp? Mạng Nội Bộ Trường Học

segments.title: Chương 79: Nhật Ký Tốt Nghiệp? Mạng Nội Bộ Trường Học
segments.content:
On the blackboard, a hundred-day countdown to the Gaokao appeared one day.

Chen Guiliang was no longer studying so frantically. He ate when he should eat, slept when he should sleep, and got his daily schedule back on track.

English vocabulary, he really didn't want to memorize it!

But he still set himself a daily goal of memorizing 15 words. On weekends, he wouldn't learn new ones, only reviewing the week's work.

Chen Guiliang wasn't going crazy, but Bian Guanyue was.

She had spent a huge amount of time on vocal music since her second year of junior high. Not to mention high school knowledge points, even her junior high knowledge was shaky. Suddenly giving up the arts exam in her third year of high school to study academic subjects, barely making it to a second-tier university in the first mock exam was already her limit.

Now that Chen Guiliang's scores were so high, and he was even aiming for Peking University, Bian Guanyue felt an inexplicable sense of panic.

After the first mock exam, Bian Guanyue barely spoke to Chen Guiliang anymore.

She usually sat in the classroom, either reading and doing problems or napping on her desk. She studied for almost fourteen hours a day.

There were even crazier ones in the class, studying sixteen hours a day!

"Keeping a clear head is more important than blindly studying," Chen Guiliang found a chance to advise. "If you study more than ten hours a day for several days straight, your brain will turn to mush."

Bian Guanyue said, "It's alright. I take short naps at my desk during breaks and the noon self-study period."

"How are you feeling?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Bian Guanyue said, "I'm improving every day. Wu Meng is amazing. She taught me a study method, and my thinking has become much clearer than before."

Wu Meng's score in the first mock exam was the highest in the entire city.

She and a certain male student from City No. 2 Middle School took turns being first. No matter how hard others tried, they could only get third.

Class president Li Rui's performance, on the other hand, was more volatile. His best score was third in the city, and his worst was ninth. He was an academic ace either way.

This was what he called volatile? Chen Guiliang chatted with Bian Guanyue for a few more sentences, then returned to his seat to study.

During this time, he paid no mind to worldly affairs, no longer bothering with newspaper opinions.

He only learned some current news, like Ah Bian being shot, when his roommates were having their nightly political discussions.

*Mengya* magazine did send another royalty payment, but it was for the first anniversary of the outbreak of the Iraq War, and tens of thousands of people worldwide were holding protests. Taking this opportunity, *Mengya* planned to publish Chen Guiliang's "Denunciation of America's Invasion of Iraq" in its next issue.

They were pretty good at riding on hot topics.

A Nokia ringtone sounded. It was Tao Chenggang calling. He probably got Chen Guiliang's new phone number from Tao Xue.

"Guiliang, congratulations on getting into Peking University," was the first thing Tao Chenggang said.

Chen Guiliang replied, "I still have to score above the first-tier university line. It's not a done deal yet."

"Getting a first-tier score will be easy for you," Tao Chenggang chatted for a bit more. "I've started a gaming company in Hangzhou."

"Hangzhou?" Chen Guiliang was quite surprised.

Tao Chenggang said, "I used to work in Hangzhou, so I'm pretty familiar with the place and know a few old friends here. UTStarcom's China headquarters is also in Hangzhou. If I run out of money later, it'll be convenient to ask my old employer for investment."

Chen Guiliang asked, "What's the company's situation now?"

"Just got the license, it's called Bailian Network Technology Co., Ltd.," Tao Chenggang said. "I brought in two partners, both are tech geniuses who used to run private servers. The game development team is temporarily set at eighteen people, and we also hired two people for miscellaneous tasks."

Chen Guiliang smiled and said, "Congratulations, congratulations. May your business prosper."

Tao Chenggang said, "I've only invested a few hundred thousand for now. I'll slowly sell the internet cafes later to raise more funds. The other two partners have also invested. They each have a 30% stake and have agreed to let me continue to inject capital later. Your shares will come from my portion. When you come to sign the papers, they'll be transferred to your name. We'll discuss the specific amount face-to-face when you sign."

"We'll talk about it then," Chen Guiliang really hadn't thought about getting involved.

Once Tao Chenggang sold off his internet cafes one by one and invested the money into the company, he would definitely dilute the partners' shares and eventually achieve absolute control over the company.

If Chen Guiliang got involved, he would only be the number four minority shareholder.

If UTStarcom invested in the future, who knew what the shareholding structure would become.

Incidentally, Shanda's new game, *Heroic Age*, was about to be launched.

Because Shanda's upper management had interfered too much with the game, intense conflicts had already broken out during the development process. With the open beta approaching, they weren't given many resources, which caused the project team to become disloyal. They were planning a mass resignation from Shanda and were already in private contact with Boss Shi.

At the end of March, there was a one-day holiday, and Chen Guiliang went home.

He had actually become a celebrity in the village. The program on Longdu News had very high viewership ratings even in rural areas.

There was no need for Chen Guiliang to publicize it himself. The whole village knew he was "guaranteed admission" to Peking University.

"Hey, the university student is back!"

"Guiliang, which is better, Peking University or Sichuan University?"

"When you graduate, you'll probably be assigned a post as an official."

"Guiliang, you're going to get an urban household registration."

"..."

The villagers' understanding of Peking University was varied and sometimes amusingly off the mark, but that didn't stop them from knowing that Peking University was a big deal.

Second Aunt's attitude had done a complete 180-degree turn. Every time she bought meat, she would buy a little extra and would definitely bring a plate over to Chen Guiliang's family.

"Grandma, I'm back."

Chen Guiliang called out. Before his grandmother could answer, the little cat darted out first.

"Meow~~"

"Get out of the way."

Grandma was busy in her private plot. She came back carrying a sickle and said, "Your mom and dad went to plant corn."

"Didn't they rent a factory building to raise rabbits?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Grandma said, "They haven't been back for seven or eight years. Some people are willing to farm the paddy fields, but more than half of the dry land has been left barren. Last month they were busy planting rice seedlings, and this month they have to clear land to plant corn. Where would they find the time to raise rabbits?"

Chen Guiliang's family land was similar to other villagers', one-third was paddy fields, and two-thirds was dry land (mostly on mountains).

No one wanted the dry land even if it was given away. After a few years, it had become hard and overgrown with weeds. Reclaiming it would work a person half to death.

Fortunately, there wasn't much of it.

The land allocated to the villagers, including both paddy and dry land, was only about 1.5 mu per person.

In the northeast and northwest regions, it wasn't uncommon for people to have tens or even hundreds of mu per person. This was unimaginable for farmers in southern Sichuan. They thought all farmers in the country only had one or two mu of land.

The sky was completely dark when his parents finally returned.

Chen Xinghua collapsed on the bed as soon as he got home, too tired to even straighten his back.

His mother, Yao Lan, asked excitedly, "Liangliang, are you really going to Peking University?"

"I definitely can," Chen Guiliang no longer spoke vaguely in front of his parents.

Chen Xinghua, lying on the bed, said, "Last week, your grandfather held a birthday banquet. Your great-grandfather, grand-uncle, grandaunt and granduncle-in-law all came. They specifically asked if you were guaranteed admission to Peking University. Your Cousin-in-law Zhong also came."

His father's tone held three parts excitement and seven parts pride.

The elders he just mentioned were all of his grandfather's relatives from the city. Chen Xinghua had been treated differently since he was a child, and this time, he was finally seen in a positive light.

Especially that Cousin-in-law Zhong, who was the second husband of Chen Xinghua's older female cousin—the number three leader of a salt factory on the verge of bankruptcy.

The salt factory was different from other state-owned enterprises. It only had the right to produce, not the right to sell or set prices. How much to produce each month, what price to sell at, and where to sell it were all dictated by higher authorities.

Redundant employees, aging equipment, and a shrinking market—all the salt factories in the city looked like they were on their last legs.

As a leader, Cousin-in-law Zhong rarely visited his rural relatives, but this time he had actually deigned to come to the banquet.

"It's fine if he came. It's good to keep in touch," Chen Guiliang said.

He knew what his father was thinking. It was simply about being looked down upon in the past and now wanting to reclaim some dignity.

His mother, Yao Lan, however, said resentfully, "We didn't keep in touch before, why are we visiting relatives now? Those city relatives of yours, even when they sent over old clothes, they let that family (Second Uncle's) pick first. We only got the leftovers they didn't want."

His father fell silent.

Chen Guiliang maintained his smile.

When he was little, he did often wear old clothes from his city relatives.

If there were old clothes for children, his younger cousin Chen Guirong got to pick first. Chen Guiliang could only take what his cousin left behind.

If all the children's old clothes were taken, he would pick from the remaining adult clothes. For example, by cutting off half the pant legs, a child could still wear them as wide-leg trousers.

Chen Guiliang wore such hand-me-downs all the way until junior high.

The situation now was that his father wanted to socialize with the city relatives. With his son's success, he would have face no matter which house he visited, making up for the grievances he suffered in his childhood.

And his mother?

She wanted nothing to do with those city relatives ever again.

Chen Guiliang didn't know whose side to take, so he simply chose to keep his mouth shut and let his parents sort it out themselves.

Yao Lan said, "Liangliang, you have to work hard for yourself. Buy a house in a big city in the future, and don't come back to the countryside. Get a big city's household registration, be even more of a city person than your dad's city relatives!"

Chen Guiliang didn't know whether to laugh or cry. In his mother's words, "city person" had become an adjective.

"Alright, I'll be more of a city person than them in the future," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Grandma didn't participate in the discussion. She quietly brought the food to the table, then held the little cat and watched TV.

She had long since become indifferent to these things.

After staying home for a night and half a day, Chen Guiliang went back to school again.

There were many exams in the third year of high school.

The second mock exam was just around the corner, and people had even started filling out graduation yearbooks.

"Great Hero Chen, you have to write something nice, preferably a poem for me!"

Qin Shanshan, his desk-mate whose father worked in the tobacco industry, slammed a yearbook down in front of Chen Guiliang.

Graduation yearbooks, such a distant memory.

Chen Guiliang stared at the thing in a daze, suddenly thinking of Xiaonei and Renren.

What year did Xiaonei go online?

Maybe I can create one during my university years.

"Hurry up and write," Qin Shanshan urged.

Chen Guiliang found it quite interesting. The yearbook was printed with all sorts of questions, like "What is your favorite color?", "Who is your favorite celebrity?", and so on.

Qin Shanshan watched him fill out the information and asked with great anticipation, "Can you write a poem?"

Chen Guiliang thought carefully for a few minutes and wrote—

To My High School Desk-mate, Qin Shanshan

By the window, we shared ink; from our pens, different worlds arose.

The days gone by are like bleeding ink on paper, and when we meet again, the words are not yet dry.

Qin Shanshan's jaw dropped, her face a picture of delighted surprise. Although she didn't recognize the character for "bleeding ink," she still thought the poem was exceptionally good.

"Haha, thanks! Here's some Alpenliebe for you."

Qin Shanshan grabbed a handful of candies for Chen Guiliang and went off to find other classmates to fill out her yearbook.

Every time she approached a classmate, she would point at Chen Guiliang's poem and say, "Look, Great Hero Chen wrote this especially for me."

This made all the classmates incredibly envious. The next day, they all rushed out to buy yearbooks, then stuffed them in front of Chen Guiliang, begging him to write a poem.

That evening, when Qin Shanshan got home, she took out her yearbook as if presenting a treasure.

"Dad, Mom, look at the poem Chen Guiliang wrote for me! I gave him my yearbook, and he wrote it in just a few minutes."

Qin Shanshan's father was the deputy section chief of the mass organizations department (the trade union office) at the tobacco company. He often had to write all sorts of documents. His eyes lit up when he saw Chen Guiliang's poem. "A true talent!"

Her mother, however, asked with some anticipation, "Does he like you? To write such a good poem for you."

Qin Shanshan rolled her eyes. "He already has a girlfriend."

Her father found a pen and paper. "I'm going to copy this down and show it to the young folks in my department tomorrow, so they can learn a thing or two. What kind of rubbish do they usually write?"

After showing off to her parents, Qin Shanshan ran to turn on her computer.

She wasn't a literary youth and didn't frequent the *Mengya* forum. She usually liked to browse and post on the Tianya forum.

Guaranteed Peking University admission genius Chen Guiliang has written a new poem!!!!

"Hehe, I'm Chen Guiliang's desk-mate. Since we're graduating soon, I asked him to fill out my yearbook and specifically asked him to write a poem. And in less than ten minutes, Great Hero Chen wrote this poem..."

Chen Guiliang had some fame on the Tianya forum, especially in the "Literature and Arts" section.

"Damn, even a casual poem is this awesome."

"So envious. I wish I had a desk-mate like that too."

"Haha, I've copied it. I'm a senior in college, going to use it for my classmates."

"OP, why do you call him Great Hero Chen?"

"The whole grade calls him Great Hero Chen. He did a lot of things even before he got famous. Last year, the third-year grade's computer class was canceled..."

"Truly the spirit of youth. No wonder he could write a line like 'Hoping this faint light will illuminate the Milky Way and all its stars'."

"Classmate Qin Shanshan, what are Chen Guiliang's usual test scores?"

"In the first mock exam a while ago, he scored 30 points above the first-tier university line."

"I thought he was weak in some subjects and his overall score wasn't good. Turns out he can get into a first-tier university based on his own ability."

"Little sis, can you ask Chen Guiliang to come to the Literature and Arts section too? We can discuss poetry with him. I'm a junior high Chinese teacher, and I taught my students *Yinghai Xing* half a month ago."

"Sure, I'll tell him. But I can't guarantee he'll come."

"..."

Qin Shanshan was listless during class but full of energy when browsing the forum. She kept reading and replying to posts late into the night.

Chen Guiliang's poem was secretly copied by many student netizens, who then passed it off as their own to show off in front of their classmates.
